title: Implement specodelic compile: Set^K -> TOML / TLA+ / proptest functor
description:
Per specs/compile.md. Translate a linted-and-covered spec file's Constraints table into a TOML document, its Model section into a TLA+ (or Alloy) module, and its Properties table into proptest! blocks — without dropping or altering any id.

MUST: ids in == ids out for every compiled file (compile_preserves_ids, no_semantic_drift); a Properties row yields a proptest! block that compiles.
METER: `spk compile <file> --json` exits 0 per file; corpus-wide demo requires specodelic-qc8 closed (precondition_satisfied demands linted+covered).
TASK LADDER (keep ticket whole per compile.md's single Compile transition): 1) Constraints→TOML, 2) Model→TLA+, 3) Properties→proptest!.
TOOLCHAIN: toml crate (already a dep); TLA+ emitted as text (checking it is nx7's job); proptest dep to add.
ANTI-GOALS: never parse prose (prose_untouched); never mint, drop, or alter ids; no orchestration logic here (that's 8kk).
REGRESSION: cargo test — tests/cli.rs + tests/spec_parse.rs keep passing (22 tests).
FILES: src/compile.rs + lib.rs wiring + main.rs Compile subcommand. New/changed files carry Purpose/Responsibilities/Rationale headers. main.rs is shared with nx7/1pv/8kk — one enum arm each; re-anchor base_commit if a sibling pipeline ticket landed first.

Depends on specodelic-qc8: the corpus must reach covered for the end-to-end demo path (compile's own precondition_satisfied).
notes: DEFERRAL (user decision): TLA+ vs Alloy backend deferred to specodelic-mp1 row 6. lnq proceeds with phases 1 (Constraints→TOML) and 3 (Properties→proptest!) + pipeline contract/CLI; model emission (phase 2) is built behind a backend-neutral seam and lands after the mp1 decision. Ticket remains open until the model artifact ships.

title: spk doctor dual-mode: workspace classification + knowledge-currency warning
description:
Approved OpenSpec change add-embedded-aix-guide (openspec/changes/add-embedded-aix-guide) — tasks.md phase 5; capability delta in specs/doctor/spec.md.

MUST: doctor classifies workspace as self_hosting (specs/specodelic.md exists) vs consumer (otherwise, incl. no specs/); self_hosting keeps today's checks; consumer mode reports embedded format_revision as ok, never fails on the missing core spec, and — when a local corpus exists — extracts its latest Revision N heading (numerically largest trailing integer) and warns (never fails) if newer than FORMAT_REVISION. Corpus with no Revision headings: skip the currency check with an informational note. Empty workspace: consumer mode with an informational spk new hint, exit 0.
METER: integration tests — self-hosting (this repo), consumer with specs dir, consumer empty, lag-warning tempdir fixture with synthetic Revision 99 corpus, marker-less corpus fixture.
ANTI-GOALS: do not invent a marker file format (Revision N headings are the marker); never let doctor exit non-zero for knowledge currency.
REGRESSION: just ci; existing doctor test (if any) updated for the mode field.
FILES: src/main.rs (cmd_doctor), src/guide.rs, tests/cli.rs.
notes: Co-modification note (review PASS 0/2): src/main.rs, src/guide.rs, tests/cli.rs are touched by 0oo/qqx/2kc — land per dep order; Revision 99 fixture must assert envelope warning + exit 0 (not informational note).

notes: Also closes tasks.md 6.3 (final slice, lands last): update README AIX section + specs/STATUS.md §3 inventory with spk explain/self-describing findings/doctor dual-mode; verify beads housekeeping (mp1 note already filed). title: Implement spk explain: embedded format guide subcommand + format_revision in version payload
description:

MUST: spk explain [TOPIC] over the genesis JSON envelope — bare call lists topics; known topic (format|ears|kinds|references|lifecycle|lint-rules) returns {topic, format_revision, body}; unknown topic exits non-zero with a hint listing valid topics. --version --json gains format_revision by hand-rolling the version envelope in main.rs from genesis::envelope::{Envelope, EnvelopeKind} — stop calling maybe_print_version_json, its payload is fixed (design.md Decision 4). Drift-guard unit test: extract Revision N headings from specs/specodelic.md, compare numerically (10 > 9), fail the suite if FORMAT_REVISION is stale.
METER: integration tests in tests/cli.rs — consumer-dir tempdir (no specs/), exact topic list, unknown-topic hint, version payload field, drift-guard double-digit case.

REGRESSION: just ci; openspec validate add-embedded-aix-guide --strict.
FILES: src/guide.rs, src/main.rs, tests/cli.rs.

Decide open spec questions before pipeline v1 (HITL)
description:
HITL ticket — human decisions required before pipeline v1 can be called done. One decision per row; each blocks CLOSING a specific ticket, not starting it.

1. rename.md Needs Human Review: is a batch (whole-namespace) rename one atomic transaction or n independent ones? → gates specodelic-ams close.
2. merge.md Needs Human Review: what does "a human has explicitly approved a flagged merge" mean operationally (review comment, CI gate, role)? → gates specodelic-7oq close.
3. refactor.md Needs Human Review: should "unrelated fan-in" key off the id namespace or physical directory placement? → gates specodelic-3l7 close.
4. orchestrate.md Needs Human Review: does the orchestrator own each file's draft→parsed transition, or stay scoped to parsed→verified? → gates specodelic-8kk close.
5. EXCL-001 (kinds.md): add a kind = "audit" property type via a Revision to specs/kinds.md (not by editing linter-schema_shape.md directly).
6. compile.md: model-checker backend for model_to_tla — TLA+ or Alloy? compile.md says "TLA+ (or Alloy)" without pinning one. Decision lands as a compile.md Revision. → gates the model-emission phase of specodelic-lnq (phases TOML/proptest proceed; ticket stays open) and nx7's checker target.

DELIVERABLE: each decision recorded where the spec says it belongs (Revision + Notes), tickets unblocked by editing their descriptions.
AFK work (lnq TOML+proptest phases, 1pv, b15, qc8) does NOT wait on this ticket.
notes: Open question partially resolved via approved OpenSpec change add-embedded-aix-guide (2026-09-28): format knowledge will be embedded in the spk binary (spk explain topics, FORMAT_REVISION pinning, self-describing lint findings, doctor dual-mode). Implementation tracked in specodelic-0oo (blocked-by root) with dependents specodelic-qqx, specodelic-2kc, specodelic-amg.

title: Complete specodelic lint: model_shape, graph_shape, reference typing, external_completeness
description:
Per specs/linter-model_shape.md, specs/linter-graph_shape.md, the Reference Typing table in specs/specodelic.md, and specs/linter-external_completeness.md — four specced checkers with no implementation, all required before orchestrate (8kk) can gate correctly.

MUST: every constraint in those four checker files has a corresponding lint rule: model_shape (every_state_used, every_transition_valid, model_sections_paired), graph_shape (acyclic, no_self_ref, single_root_reachable, supersedes_dag), reference typing (ref_kind_compatible — advisory/effect constraints can never gate; emits→effect only; supersedes same-kind), external_completeness (checklist_well_formed, covered_maps_resolve, every_item_accounted, no_duplicate_claim, waiver_has_rationale — optional, non-gating).
METER: `spk lint specs --json` reports zero findings for those rules on the corpus (new known-issues list replaces today's); synthetic fixtures prove each rule fires.
ANTI-GOALS: never parse prose; never add rules the checker specs don't state; external_completeness never gates a stage.
REGRESSION: cargo test — existing suites keep passing.
FILES: src/lint.rs (and src/graph.rs if reachability helpers are shared). File-header required.

title: Implement specodelic merge: id collisions + dangling renames pre-merge
description:
Per specs/merge.md. Detect what a textual git merge can't see: id collisions between branches and renames left dangling by references minted elsewhere, before reporting a merge complete.

MUST: a two-branch fixture with an id collision is flagged; a rename left dangling by a reference minted on the other branch is flagged; a clean merge reports no findings.
METER: integration test with two tempdir spec trees + `spk merge --json` findings; cargo test.
ANTI-GOALS: don't re-derive the reference graph (graph_reused_not_rederived — consume graph.rs); don't gate on findings the spec doesn't gate on.
HITL: what "a human has explicitly approved a flagged merge" means operationally — see specodelic-mp1 before closing.
FILES: src/merge.rs; reuse graph.rs. File-header required.

title: Implement specodelic orchestrate: lint->compile->model_check->verify driver
description:
Per specs/orchestrate.md. Drive the six Checker Ownership checkers in dependency order (skip dependents on failure, run independent branches regardless), then coverage, compile, model_check, verify in sequence — gating each stage transition on the exact guards specs/specodelic.md specifies, never looser or stricter. external_completeness runs when a checklist exists but never gates. rename stays out of scope.

MUST: a corpus run reports each stage's outcome; the first failing stage halts its dependents (skipped, not failed) while independent branches still report; stage sequence matches specodelic.md's lifecycle (draft → parsed → linted → compiled → model_checked → verified).
METER: `spk orchestrate specs --json` → .data lists every stage with status; halt/skip behavior proven by a synthetic fixture with one failing checker.
ANTI-GOALS: no looser/stricter gating than specified; no rename triggering; no silent skips (every skip is reported).
REGRESSION: cargo test — existing suites keep passing.
FILES: src/orchestrate.rs + main.rs Orchestrate subcommand (file-header required; shared main.rs with sibling pipeline tickets).

Depends on specodelic-1pv (last pipeline stage) and specodelic-b15 (all six Checker Ownership checkers must exist first). HITL: whether the orchestrator also owns draft→parsed — see specodelic-mp1 before closing.

title: Implement specodelic rename: atomic id rename with link rewrite
description:
Per specs/rename.md. Single (old_id, new_id) request: update the defining row and every referencing [[link]] atomically, or leave the repo unchanged. Ends in a verify step re-running linter.referential_integrity and linter.graph_shape (i.e. `spk graph` + `spk lint` — the linters, NOT the pipeline verify command).

MUST: after a successful rename, `spk graph specs --json` .data.dangling length == 0 and the new id resolves everywhere the old one did; on a failed precondition every file is byte-identical to before (all-or-nothing).
METER: rename integration test on a tempdir fixture (definition + cross-file links) + the graph check above.
ANTI-GOALS: no partial renames (atomicity is the point); batch/whole-namespace rename out of scope pending HITL (rename.md Needs Human Review — see specodelic-mp1).
REGRESSION: cargo test — existing suites keep passing.
FILES: src/rename.rs; reuse graph.rs (do not re-derive). File-header required.

Builds on the existing graph command (done).

title: Implement specodelic verify: execute proptest blocks + gate
description:
Per specs/verify.md. Run every proptest! block compile produced to completion; transition a file to verified only when all pass AND model_check's most recent run against the CURRENT compiled artifact is clean.

MUST: a file with a failing proptest block is NOT verified; a file whose model_check result is stale (artifact changed since the run) is NOT verified; only the conjunction verifies.
METER: `spk verify <file> --json` → .data.status == "verified" exactly in that case, else the blocking stage is named.
ANTI-GOALS: never bypass the model_check guard; never cache/assume artifacts are current; never treat a skipped stage as passed.
REGRESSION: cargo test — existing suites keep passing.
FILES: src/verify.rs + main.rs Verify subcommand (file-header required; shared main.rs with sibling pipeline tickets).

Depends on specodelic-lnq (proptest blocks) and specodelic-nx7 (clean-run guard).

title: Implement specodelic model-check: TLC/Alloy against compiled module
description:
Per specs/model_check.md. Run a model checker (TLC or Alloy) against compile's TLA+ output; report no_counterexample-within-bound or a minimal counterexample trace naming the violated invariant. Distinguish model_checked (a run happened) from no_counterexample (no violation found) — CLAR-003.

MUST: a synthetic spec with a violated invariant yields a counterexample trace naming the invariant; a clean spec reports no_counterexample within the stated bound; a missing checker binary is an ERROR, never a no_counterexample result.
METER: `spk model-check <file> --json` → .data.outcome ∈ {"no_counterexample","counterexample"}.
TOOLCHAIN (pick ONE for v0 and record the choice + binary pin in specs/model_check.md Notes): TLC (Java + tlc2.sh) or Alloy (alloy.jar).
ANTI-GOALS: never re-compile inside model-check (consume compile's artifact); never collapse "checker not installed" into "no counterexample".
REGRESSION: cargo test — existing suites keep passing.
FILES: src/model_check.rs + main.rs ModelCheck subcommand (file-header required; shared main.rs with sibling pipeline tickets).

Depends on specodelic-lnq (consumes its TLA+ output).

description:

title: Implement specodelic refactor: tidy-first split advisor
description:
Per specs/refactor.md. Flag nodes with high, unrelated fan-in in the reference graph as tidy-first split candidates. Always non-gating (kind == effect, already excluded from every guard by the format's typing — no new "never gates" invariant needed).

MUST: a synthetic node with high unrelated fan-in is flagged; a node with coherent fan-in is not; output is advisory only (exit 0 either way).
METER: `spk refactor specs --json` on a synthetic fixture; cargo test.
ANTI-GOALS: never gate a pipeline stage on this advisory; don't invent a new invariant where the typing table already excludes effect constraints from guards.
HITL: whether "unrelated" keys off id namespace or directory placement — see specodelic-mp1 (flat namespace convention would make the advisory fire on almost everything).
FILES: src/refactor.rs; reuse graph.rs. File-header required.
